A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original active-testing experiments, including risk-estimation comparisons, surrogate-model analyses, label-filtering experiments and bootstrap coverage measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a dynamic-versus-fixed surrogate comparison in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The proposed fixed in-context surrogate, LURE estimator, acquisition functions and bootstrap error estimator remain unchanged. Dynamic surrogate updating is introduced as an experimental comparator in Appendix C.5, rather than a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST-2, Subj, FPB, HS and four-choice MMLU, including the existing curation and label-filtering scenarios. The new dynamic-surrogate experiment reuses four existing datasets. Correcting the MMLU citation does not establish a dataset replacement.

E2.justification: v2 adds dynamically updated LURE-7B as a comparator against fixed LURE-7B and uniform-random testing in Tables 5–6. Existing uniform-random, ASE and surrogate-model comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new Appendix C.5 experiment starts with 10 in-context examples, runs 40 acquisition steps and reports mean squared error, whereas the retained main experiments use median squared error. The stated Subj source training-set size also changes from 8,000 to 10,000, retaining the 6,000/4,000 split; this documents a correction without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a focused ablation testing whether updating the surrogate context improves estimation over keeping it fixed, across four datasets and two target models. Existing small-surrogate, MMLU, label-noise, correlation and bootstrap analyses remain, although reorganized.

E5.justification: The new dynamic-surrogate comparison specifies 50 seeds for dynamic testing and 3,000 for fixed and uniform-random testing, and reports 5th/95th percentile intervals. These are newly reported experimental statistics, not evidence of increased runs for existing experiments. The original 100-run, 1,000-bootstrap-estimate analysis is unchanged.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark tables have unchanged numerical entries. New Tables 5–6 report mixed dynamic-surrogate results: for 70B-few at step 40, dynamic versus fixed MSE multiplied by 10^4 is 11.10 versus 33.25 on FPB, but 64.43 versus 47.24 on Subj. Section 5.6 also revises the existing FPB curation finding from roughly matching random sampling to performing slightly worse.

T1.justification: The risk definitions, LURE/ASE equations, acquisition functions and bootstrap variance derivation retain their mathematical substance. The non-independent-loss caveat and absence of bootstrap convergence guarantees are also retained; changes are explanatory or typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: computationally cheaper active testing with fixed, potentially smaller surrogates, optional avoidance of target predictions during acquisition, and a single-run bootstrap diagnostic. The principal improvement and coverage claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of the dynamic-surrogate comparison as supporting the computational tradeoff of fixing the surrogate. Section 5.2 overstates this as providing no accuracy benefits, despite improvements in some Table 5–6 settings. The weak-surrogate discussion also replaces v1's emphasis on graceful failure and robustness with a more restrained warning that weak surrogates can undermine active testing.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub repository and documents context updating and prediction recomputation for the new dynamic comparison. Existing quantization, prompts, token processing, acquisition clipping and GPU-count disclosures are substantially retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Settles (2012) and an explanation for excluding active-learning acquisition methods as baselines, corrects the main-text MMLU citation, and removes references to MMLU-Pro, AGIEval and frontier dangerous-capability evaluation. The central positioning relative to previous active-testing and dataset-curation research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision extensively edits the abstract, introduction and explanatory prose, adds numbered background subsections, reorganizes implementation details and supplementary analyses, and changes numerical citations to author-year citations. It also adds acknowledgements and the NeurIPS checklist. These constitute substantial editorial and structural revision beyond the added experiment.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are extensively reformatted and redistributed. Figure 3 expands from a small wrapped figure to full width; v1 Figure 5 becomes separate Figures 5–6; Figures C.1–C.2 merge into Figure 10. Tables receive redesigned headings, rules and captions, existing results are relocated, and new Tables 5–6 present the dynamic comparison.

improvement.justification: The new dynamic-versus-fixed ablation supplies useful evidence about a central design choice, with seed counts and percentile intervals, while the revised presentation improves readability. These are modest gains because the main empirical evidence is unchanged. A material weakness is Section 5.2's claim of no accuracy benefits from dynamic updating: Tables 5–6 show benefits in some settings, so the new evidence supports a more qualified conclusion.
